cases.question: Differentiate f(x) = x³ sin x.
cases.reference: By the product rule, f'(x) = 3x² sin x + x³ cos x.

answers.label: correct
answers.text: By the product rule, f'(x) = (x³)' sin x + x³ (sin x)' = 3x² sin x + x³ cos x.

cases.question: Compute the determinant of the matrix [[2, 1, 3], [0, 4, 1], [5, 2, 0]].
A test for a disease has 99% sensitivity and 95% specificity. The prevalence is 1%. What is the probability that a person who tests positive actually has the disease?

answers.label: correct_alt_method
answers.text: Take 10,000 people: 100 have the disease, of whom 99 test positive; 9,900 do not, of whom 5% = 495 test positive. P(D|+) = 99/(99 + 495) = 99/594 = 1/6 ≈ 0.167.

cases.question: Prove that 1 + 2 + ... + n = n(n+1)/2 for all positive integers n.
cases.reference: Base case n = 1: LHS = 1, RHS = 1·2/2 = 1. Inductive step: assume 1 + ... + k = k(k+1)/2. Then 1 + ... + k + (k+1) = k(k+1)/2 + (k+1) = (k+1)(k/2 + 1) = (k+1)(k+2)/2, which is the formula for n = k+1. By induction the formula holds for all n ≥ 1.

cases.question: Prove that sec(2π/9) + sec(4π/9) + sec(8π/9) = 6.
cases.reference:
Let x = 2cosθ. Then x³ − 3x = 8cos³θ − 6cosθ = 2cos3θ, so x³ − 3x + 1 = 0 exactly when cos3θ = −1/2. For θ = 2π/9, 4π/9, 8π/9 we have 3θ = 2π/3, 4π/3, 8π/3, and cos of each is −1/2. Hence r₁ = 2cos(2π/9), r₂ = 2cos(4π/9), r₃ = 2cos(8π/9) are roots of x³ − 3x + 1. Since cos is strictly decreasing on [0, π] and the three angles lie in [0, π], the rᵢ are distinct, so they are all three roots of the cubic.

By Vieta on the monic cubic x³ + 0·x² − 3x + 1: r₁ + r₂ + r₃ = 0, r₁r₂ + r₂r₃ + r₃r₁ = −3, r₁r₂r₃ = −1. Therefore
1/r₁ + 1/r₂ + 1/r₃ = (r₁r₂ + r₂r₃ + r₃r₁)/(r₁r₂r₃) = (−3)/(−1) = 3.
Finally secθᵢ = 1/cosθᵢ = 2/rᵢ, so sec(2π/9) + sec(4π/9) + sec(8π/9) = 2 · 3 = 6.
